subject: Territory-binding affirmation and PrivateLink operations checklist
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@healthgrid.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: territorial hosting affirmation + PrivateLink ops checklist

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this — our security team is finalizing controls for an EU-bound deployment and we need a short, signed acknowledgement from Redwood confirming a few items before we proceed to procurement: 

1) A written statement that customer production data for HealthGrid will remain hosted within the EU region (list regions explicitly if possible).
2) Confirmation that PrivateLink/privatelink-style connectivity will be used for private peering and that there are named operator contacts for peering and failover.
3) High-level network egress/egress-control information (what third-party egress destinations exist if any).
4) A pointer to your recent SOC 2 / CAIQ artifacts or a SIG status summary; if any items are restricted, please flag them.

We'd appreciate a single PDF 'ops checklist' that we can share with Legal and Infrastructure — a one-pager + attachments is ideal. Can you also include a timeline for a canary traffic test once peering is up?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Security Operations
HealthGrid

Attachment: none
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: territorial hosting affirmation + PrivateLink ops checklist

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide the materials. Summary below and attached is the ops packet we typically share for EU-bound customers.

What we've provided in the attached packet (redwood_vpc_peering_topology.pdf + hosting_commitment_letter_signed.pdf):
- Hosting boundary: production model serving and customer data will be deployed to our EU (eu-west-1 and eu-central-1) tenant pools. We will not route customer production inference traffic outside of the EU region for the pinned environment described in the commitment letter.
- Connectivity: PrivateLink-style peering using dedicated VPC endpoints and tenant-isolated routes. The ops checklist includes primary and standby operator contacts (see section 'Peering contacts').
- Egress: Outbound calls to third-party telemetry endpoints are disabled by default on dedicated/private deployments. There are a few controlled egress paths for managed patching and image signing (listed in the network appendix). Those are limited to vendor update services and are TLS-only.
- Compliance artifacts: we have included a SIG status summary and a pointer to our SOC 2 report access process. Per standard practice, full SOC 2 report delivery is gated by an NDA; we can expedite on request.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached checklist and confirm the operator contact you'd like us to use for peering coordination.
- We can run a 2-hour canary test (low-volume synthetic traffic) within 3 business days after peering is established; ben can own the technical plan.

Attaching: redwood_vpc_peering_topology.pdf (Topology + endpoint names), hosting_commitment_letter_signed.pdf (signed letter), Drive link to detailed diagrams.

If you want anything redacted or need on-company-letterhead formatting for procurement, let me know and I can route to Legal.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Aisha Rahman | redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_vpc_peering_topology.pdf (PDF), hosting_commitment_letter_signed.pdf (PDF)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: territorial hosting affirmation + PrivateLink ops checklist

Hi Liam — quick technical clarifications and evidence items we included: 

- Network flows: see network_flow_diagram.svg (attached) — shows peering endpoints, explicit deny by default on egress subnets, and control-plane traffic paths that are pinned to EU routing tables.
- KMS: customer data is encrypted at rest using tenant-specific keys; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and we've attached a keystore_partition_statement.txt describing logical separation.
- Operator contacts: primary peering engineer: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.ai), backup: Marissa Cole. Both can be added to your peering ticket and will have access restricted to the peering project.
- Canary plan: propose a four-step canary (provision, low-rate inference, latency checks, scale up) — estimated 2 hours for the low-rate phase, 6 hours for full ramp if you want progressive verification. We will provide a short runbook for each step.

Attached: network_flow_diagram.svg, keystore_partition_statement.txt. If you need packet captures for peering verification, we can provide sample meta-logs once the peer is established (we do not provide customer payloads).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if any of these need finer detail.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: network_flow_diagram.svg (SVG), keystore_partition_statement.txt (TXT)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthgrid.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@healthgrid.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: territorial hosting affirmation + PrivateLink ops checklist

Aisha/Ben — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick notes from Compliance: 

- The signed hosting commitment letter is sufficient for procurement — we will attach it to the order.
- Please confirm the exact peering operator contact phone for on-call escalation (we have the emails).
- Confirm you will disable outbound telemetry to non-EU domains during the pilot (you noted disabled by default; we need explicit confirmation for the EU tenant).
- Can you confirm an exact earliest date you can start the canary? We are aiming for next Tuesday (2026-12-08) window.

If you can reply with the phone number and canary start date by EOD tomorrow, we can trigger procurement and network tickets.

Cheers,
Liam
